claims.text: 16-year-old male with allergic rhinitis had fever, odynophagia and exudative tonsillitis with a truncal rash; a first streptococcal antigen test and EBV serology were negative and he improved. A week later fever recurred, the streptococcal antigen test was positive and amoxicillin was started. On day nine of amoxicillin a morbilliform exanthem developed, with positive EBV VCA IgM and IgG, and he improved on antihistamine therapy. Oral provocation 10 weeks later reproduced a morbilliform rash, confirming amoxicillin hypersensitivity.

claims.text: 12-year-old female with fever, odynophagia, abdominal pain and nausea for six days on amoxicillin with positive streptococcal antigen test was admitted on day nine of amoxicillin with generalized maculopapular rash including palms and soles, arthralgia and right tibiotarsal swelling, raised liver enzymes and positive EBV VCA IgM and IgG. Probable serum sickness-like illness resolved after stopping amoxicillin with antihistamines, and liver enzymes normalized at three weeks. Oral provocation 11 weeks later produced a generalized urticarial rash and right wrist edema.
